scope: R143 in-model staging alignment: copy-stream prefetch span vs compute-stream block start/end
interpretation: Each block runs about 348 ms while its successor weight copy spans about 60 ms and completes roughly 315 ms into the current block, so the copy finishes only about 33 ms before the next block begins. Staging is therefore just-in-time with a small margin, and the copy runs concurrently with compute rather than idling.
open_question: the 5.6x in-model vs standalone qkv gap is not explained by waiting for the copy to start; the candidates are the block pre-hook weight materialisation and HBM contention from the concurrent copy
scope_correction: this baseline replay step measures 18.07 s, matching R126s 17.946 s baseline receipt rather than the 19.906 s seen under the R140 profile-mode hooks
median_prefetch_over_h2d_floor: per block weights are 32.28 GB / 50 = 0.646 GB; at the measured 21.8 GB/s pure rate that is 29.6 ms, so the observed 60 ms span is about 2x the pure-transfer floor, consistent with contention
